segments.name: Midnight dApp teams
segments.who: Teams writing Compact contracts, from buildathon projects to production apps.
segments.need: To know what a contract gives away before it is deployed and its history is public for good.
segments.gets: The scanner, CLI and GitHub Action, free. Findings on the pull request with the fix inline. A README badge.
segments.pays: Private repositories: the hosted pull-request bot.

segments.name: Audit firms
segments.who: Security firms reviewing Compact contracts for clients.
segments.need: A fast, repeatable map of every disclosure, per circuit and field, to start a review and to attach to a report.
segments.gets: Bulk scanning, the per-circuit disclosure map, and reports in SARIF and Markdown to cite in a review.

segments.name: Midnight Foundation and templates
segments.who: The people who maintain Midnight's examples, project templates and developer programs.
segments.need: New apps that are private by default, not only by intent.
segments.gets: A Tell check in the templates and examples, rule research, and support for each new compiler release on the day it ships.

segments.name: Wallets and dApp stores
segments.who: Wallets that show a contract before a user signs, and directories that list Midnight apps.
segments.need: Something simple to tell users about an app's privacy before they use it.
segments.gets: Read access to the privacy grade registry on chain: one lookup by contract address.
segments.pays: Nothing. Reading grades is free, because grades that users can see are what make teams want a good one.

segments.name: AI coding agents
segments.who: Developers who write Compact with an AI assistant.
segments.need: An agent that checks its own contract before suggesting it.
segments.gets: An MCP server: scan, explain a finding and propose a fix, as tools an agent can call.
segments.pays: Nothing for the public tools. Agents on private code use the hosted service.

offers.name: Open-source core
offers.what: The analyzer, every rule, the CLI, the GitHub Action, the web scanner, the leak zoo and the README badge.
offers.priceNote: Always free. Public repositories never pay.

offers.name: Hosted pull-request bot
offers.what: Tell as a GitHub App on private repositories: a comment on each pull request with the findings, the verified fix and the grade change, plus history per contract.
includes: Fix suggestions on the pull request
offers.priceNote: Planned price, to test with the first pilot; public repositories stay free.

offers.name: Audit-firm license
offers.what: Bulk scans, a privacy section ready to drop into a review, and early access to new rules.
includes: Rule updates for each compiler release
offers.priceNote: Pilot price we are testing; the first engagement is free.

offers.name: Ecosystem sponsorship
offers.what: Funds rule research, support for each compiler release and a Tell check in Midnight's templates. Everything it produces stays open source.
offers.priceNote: A 12-month maintenance grant; everything it pays for stays open source.

offers.name: Grade attestations (Tell Desk)
offers.what: A team files a sealed report and an on-chain grade for a contract; wallets and stores read it.
offers.priceNote: Writing grades is part of the audit and pull-request offers.

principles.title: Public code is always free
principles.text: Every rule, the CLI, the Action and the scanner stay Apache-2.0. A paid tier never hides a finding from a public repository.

principles.title: Pay for the hosting, not the analyzer
principles.text: Money comes from things that cost us to run, like private repositories, history and bulk scans. It does not come from locking the analysis.

principles.title: Honest labels
principles.text: Every offer on this page says whether it is live, in a pilot or planned. Prices appear once they are set.
